events.title: Coffee Concert: Fantasies for Two
events.location: Main Stage at Surrey Arts Centre 13750 88 Ave
events.description: The Bergmann Duo is delighted to return to Surrey with the captivating programme Fantasies for Two . This special concert showcases some of their favourite works from the piano four-hands repertoire on two pianos. The programme features the magnificent and deeply moving Fantasy in F minor by Franz Schubert, alongside Marcel Bergmann’s own imaginative Fantasy on Gershwin’s Porgy and Bess , inspired by the music of George Gershwin. Get tickets About the Bergmann Duo The Bergmann Duo’s dynamic and energetic performances of uniquely eclectic programmes, which include numerous own arrangements and compositions, have inspired audiences internationally. They have performed in concert and with orchestra in: Canada, the USA, Italy, Germany, The Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, France, Macedonia, Greece and China. The duo has appeared at the: Festival of the Sound, Ottawa International Chamber Music Festival, Abbey Bach Festival,Tuckamore Festival, Ohrid Summer Festival, Zodiac Festival, San Francisco International Music Festival, MusicFest Vancouver, Gilmore International Keyboard Festival, Banff Arts Festival, Royal Bank Calgary International Organ Festival and Competition, Festival Miami, Tage für Neue Musik, Darmstadt, Braunschweiger Kammermusik Podium, and EXPO 2000, Hannover. They have made recordings for the CBC, ARD(in Germany) and for National Public Radio and have recorded several CDs (CordAria, Arktos, Koch International Classics, Naxos, ARS and Brilliant Classics labels). The married couple received first prize at the International Chamber Music Competition in Caltanissetta, Italy, were laureates of The 4th Murray Dranoff International Two Piano Competition and have performed extensively in Germany as members of the young artists’ roster of Yehudi Menuhin-Live Music Now. The duo studied with Arie Vardi at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater, Hannover and with Jean-Eudes Vaillancourt at the Université de Montréal. Elizabeth is Artistic Director of Concerts at the Langley Community Music School and both are Artistic Directors of White Rock Concerts.

events.description: About the event Do you have experience working with the community? Are you curious what this could look like? This event will focus on the joys of welcoming other people into your artistic practice, as well as the ethics and logistics of working with community members. Artists Joan Williams, Mariel Nels, and Carmen Rosen will discuss how they each engage with community to produce artwork and build relationships. No matter what artistic practice you engage in—visual art, performing art, storytelling, photography, etc.—bring your insights and questions; let's talk about what it means to engage with community-led practices! About the speakers Joan Williams is a contemporary Indigenous artist and member of the Semiahmoo First Nation who studied at the Art Institute of Vancouver. Her multidisciplinary practice spans weaving, drawing, and digital arts, blending traditional Coast Salish motifs with modern techniques. Her expansive practice regulary incorporates community engagement. Mariel Nelms works at the intersection of participatory art, visual storytelling, photography, and material exploration. Her practice centers on creating accessible, collaborative art experiences that invite people to engage in making as a way of connecting. Carmen Rosen is an artist, singer, community organizer, and Founding Artistic Director of Still Moon Arts Society. Her creative projects are focused on the Still Creek Watershed in her Renfrew-Collingwood neighbourhood and work within themes of nature, environmental sustainability and the love of working with people and community. What to expect Opportunity to connect with fellow Surrey artists of all disciplines. Meet and interact with community-engaged creatives. Meet City staff from our Civic Theatres and Community Arts teams. Learn about artist opportunities and spaces offered by the City.

events.title: Inouye Park Heritage Unveiling
events.location: Inouye Park, 9158 134 Street, Surrey
events.description: More than a mailbox Join us in Inouye Park as we unveil a new heritage feature recognizing the experiences and contributions of early Japanese Canadian residents in Surrey. The new feature includes the artwork “Konjou” by artist Kellen Hatanaka and interpretive features that share the story of Zennosuke Inouye. The unveiling marks the first of a three-point public heritage project that also includes a commemorative feature in RA Nicholson Park, and a permanent large-scale photo display at the Strawberry Hill Hall. Together they highlight the significant contributions of early Japanese Canadians in Surrey, as well as the injustice of their dispossession and internment during and after World War II. We gratefully acknowledge support from the Japanese Canadian Legacies Society About the artwork: Konjou Meaning perseverance in Japanese, “Konjou” honours the history and legacy of Zennosuke Inouye in the form of a mailbox. After being interned, Mr. Inouye fought to reclaim his property through a personal letter writing campaign. The mailbox symbolizes home and land ownership and represents the rural farming community that existed in the Strawberry Hill area. Accompanying the mailbox is a Japanese rock garden, honouring the history of Japanese Canadians utilizing stones to create monuments inspired by Japanese garden design. About the artist: Kellen Hatanaka A Japanese Canadian multidisciplinary artist, Kellen Hatanaka works in a variety of mediums, including painting, sculpture and public art. His work considers race, tradition, and heritage as he explores personal and collective identity and the nuances of the Japanese Canadian experience through sport, design, history and culture. Who was Zennosuke Inouye? Zennosuke Inouye and his family owned a successful farm in Strawberry Hill until, in 1942, the Canadian government forced all people of Japanese ancestry to leave the west coast. They later sold Japanese Canadian possessions without permission from the owners. After writing dozens of letters to government officials reminding them of his service to Canada in WW1, the government returned his land to him in 1949. Of the 60 interned families in the area, the Inouye's were the only one to have their land returned. Photo credit: Zennosuke Inouye Farm; Surrey, BC. Ca. 1930. Beverly Inouye Collection. Nikkei National Museum & Cultural Centre 1994.83.8.

events.description: “ If Dizzy Gillespie were still with us, he would love CaneFire ”—Vancouver Sun Toronto-based Caribbean jazz powerhouse CaneFire is NOT your grandfather’s jazz band. As one of the most explosive and energetic jazz ensembles on the planet, CaneFire delivers a rollicking, high-octane show combining the white-hot energy of Cuban rhythm, the blinding musicianship of modern jazz, and the unbridled joy of the music of the Caribbean. CaneFire’s signature sound revolves around its unconventional use of the steelpan—the only petroleum byproduct in the world that is actually good for you. Led by Canadian pianist/composer Jeremy Ledbetter , CaneFire also features steelpan virtuoso Mark Mosca , Alexis Baro (trumpet), Braxton Hicks (saxophones), Chendy Leon (drums), Yoser Rodriguez (bass), and Alberto Suarez (percussion). CaneFire has released two albums and taken their unique brand of Caribbean Latin Jazz from BC to Newfoundland, to South America, and to the Caribbean, including three years in a row at the Trinidad and Tobago Jazz Festival. Their second album Pandemonium embodies all the sizzle and twice the sophistication of its predecessor and features guest performances by Trinidadian calypso superstar David Rudder and Brazilian jazz legend, Hermeto Pascoal. events.title: Cabaret of Legends
events.location: Main Stage Surrey Arts Centre, 13750 88 Ave, Surrey, BC
events.description: A stunning display of song and history… 5 STARS” Edmonton Journal A Dynamite Lunchbox Production CREATED BY TYMISHA HARRIS AND MICHAEL MARINACCIO Step into an electrifying, genre-blending musical experience that celebrates the power, soul, and legacy of Black female icons. Cabaret of Legends stars international award-winning vocalist and performer Tymisha Harris , whose powerhouse voice and captivating storytelling bring history to life on stage. From the jazz brilliance of Ella Fitzgerald and Billie Holiday to the revolutionary spirit of Nina Simone , the fire of Tina Turner , and the unforgettable vocals of Whitney Houston and Beyoncé , this show is a dynamic tribute spanning a century of legendary music. Fans of Tymisha Harris’ acclaimed hit Josephine will be thrilled—this is a performance that inspires, uplifts, and delivers unforgettable moments from start to finish. Don’t miss your chance to experience this extraordinary celebration of music and storytelling—secure your tickets today! Buy tickets About Tymisha Harris Tymisha Harris is a dynamic and versatile vocalist with a career spanning four decades. Her early credits include work with *NSYNC, LFO, Universal Studios Orlando, and the Bring It On movie series. She has also starred in national and international tours of Rock of Ages , Pilobolus Dance Theatre Company, and her own off-Broadway hit, Josephine .

events.title: Coffee Concert: Percussiano 3
events.location: Studio Theatre at Surrey Arts Centre; 13750 - 88 - Avenue, Surrey, BC
events.description: Percussiano 3 brings together the Bergmann Duo and percussionist Rod Thomas Squance in a dynamic six-hand performance. Blending piano four hands with a vibrant array of percussion, the programme spans from Bach to Piazzolla, and includes a new arrangement of Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue , creating an electrifying and genre-crossing concert experience. Includes the ever-popular pre-show social hour! This show is part of the Coffee Concert Series. Buy tickets About the Bergmann Duo Elizabeth and Marcel Bergmann have been performing together as a duo since 1989, and their dynamic and energetic performances of uniquely eclectic programs have inspired audiences for more than two decades. The duo, who are laureates of the Dranoff International Two Piano Competition, perform a wide variety of repertoire and styles, and enjoy dazzling audiences around the world at festivals and on tour. Their recitals and concerts with orchestras have taken them all over the world, including the United States, Italy, Germany, Holland, Greece, and Canada. Rod Thomas Squance A stunning soloist, percussionist Rod captivates audiences with his perfect blend of compelling musicianship, sparkling technique, and exotic sound. He has performed with Yo-Yo Ma and the Silk Road Project, Paquito de Rivera, Dong-Won Kim, Kojiro Umezaki, Yu Hongmei and Prafulla Athalye. Rod has appeared on national radio and television, solo recitals and with many orchestras. Classically trained, Rod also plays jazz vibraphone, Balinese shadow-puppet music and Indian classical music. He currently teaches at the University of Calgary.

events.title: How to Catch a Star
events.location: Main Stage at Surrey Arts Centre 13750 88 Avenue, Surrey, BC
events.description: By Branar Téatar do Pháistí (Ireland) Once there was a boy who was always looking up. He dreamt of having a star as a friend. This is the story of his adventure. Based on the beloved book by award-winning Irish author Oliver Jeffers. This adaptation combines stunning puppetry with a twinkling musical score and Branar’s signature storytelling that reminds us all to follow our dreams. A non-verbal show for ages 4+. Get tickets About Branar Téatar do Pháistí Based in the West of Ireland since 2001, Branar is one of Ireland’s leading theatre companies making work for children. Renowned for creating highly imaginative and beautiful work, Branar tours nationally and internationally. Their company’s motto is ‘serious fun’. Aiming to instill not just wildness inside us but wonder, joy, curiosity and compassion, Branar views every child as an equal citizen of the world who should be nurtured through engagement with exceptional arts experiences. Filled with wonder and creativity, their world and the world around them will be more fulfilling for all. The company tours nationally and internationally, bringing its work with equal enthusiasm to leading arts venues such as the South Bank Centre, London as to a local school in Galway. Branar is committed to reaching its audience, wherever they are. Kindly supported by Culture Ireland, Arts Council of Ireland, Galway City Council, Foras na Gaeilge and Galway County Council.
